evidence: Mechanics are as described: in the frozen tree (a7fb363b) products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:222 imports `products.stamphog.backend.facade.api.queue_inbox_pr_review` one line above `try:` (224), whose `except Exception` (238) would not cover an ImportError, and both `transaction.on_commit` registrations (receivers.py:116, 129) omit `robust=`, so under Django 5.2.14 (uv.lock:1783) a hook raising inside an atomic block propagates out of the outermost atomic exit after commit (django/db/backends/base/base.py:752-769). But the import cannot fail in a running process: `products.stamphog.backend` is in INSTALLED_APPS (posthog/settings/web.py:45), its models.py:18 imports `.facade.enums` during django.setup(), receivers.py:53 imports `products.stamphog.backend.facade.inbox_hooks` at module top from `ReviewHogConfig.ready()` (apps.py:11-13), and facade/api.py:11-13 imports only `..models`, `.contracts` (pydantic) and `.enums` - every dependency is first-party and already loaded before any save can fire; the heavy Celery/GitHub/temporal import is deferred inside `queue_inbox_pr_review` itself (api.py:147), i.e. inside the try. The module is also imported at module level by products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:16 and patched by name in tests/test_inbox_trigger.py:24. Neither production writer of `output.pr_url`/`head_branch` would surface an error anyway: the agent-server path `set_task_run_output` (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2153-2154) saves outside any atomic block, so on_commit runs the lambda inline (base.py:737-750) inside the receiver's own `except Exception` (receivers.py:140-141); the webhook backstop `_record_run_output_field` (products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:286-298) wraps its atomic save in `try/except Exception` that logs and returns False. So 'return an error for a successful TaskRun write' has no reachable trigger at this commit; the only precondition is a deployment in which a first-party module is unimportable, which breaks django.setup() everywhere first.
notes: The opposite verdict would need facade/api.py (or something it imports) to be optional, settings-gated, or subject to a first-call circular import, plus a production saver that both runs inside an atomic block and does not catch exceptions from the atomic exit; none of those hold in the frozen tree. Moving the import inside the try changes nothing observable. Relation to NA20: NA20 (real, consider) already covers the general defect that both hooks are non-robust and ReviewHog-first, so a slow Temporal connect or failure in `_start_review` delays or prevents the Stamphog dispatch; `robust=True` on both registrations is the fix for that class, and it would also subsume PB14's hypothetical. PB14 adds nothing beyond NA20 - it is at most a style nit about import placement, not a distinct failure.
